open_errors.issue: Madhavi, a Resin House member who knows the witness rule, says the queen can cage the forty without a page. The queen never witnessed any of the forty turn, so she cannot cage them. Nobody corrects the claim.
open_errors.fix: Change Madhavi's claim from caging to keeping.

patches.find: She doesn't need a page to cage *us*, if we walk in.
patches.replace: She won't need a page to keep *us*, once we've walked in.

open_errors.issue: Ch 6 says the five go south 'at the next light'. In ch 7, the following day, Neela says they leave at first light, and in ch 8 they set off a day later than ch 6 states.

patches.find: Pavi and the others would go south at the next light.
patches.replace: Pavi and the others would go south as soon as the gorge let them.

open_errors.issue: The long-table memory has Neela at nine. Ch 29 and continuity (F232, F493) place the same scene at ten.

patches.find: For an instant she was nine years old on a bench with her feet not reaching the floor
patches.replace: For an instant she was ten years old on a bench with her feet not reaching the floor

open_errors.issue: In ch 15 Neela pricks her thumb half an hour before the noon gun so that Devan gets an early signal (F857). In ch 14, the same hour, Devan reasons as if no welts reached him at all.
open_errors.fix: Have Devan register the early welts without understanding them.

patches.find: He counted the hour, too. It was well past noon by the sun, and he had not pricked his thumb.
patches.replace: He counted the hour, too. It was well past noon by the sun, and he had not pricked his thumb. Hers had come early, three small stings on the climb, a half hour short of noon, and he had not known what early meant.

open_errors.issue: Continuity F877 and F880 say Kuttu asked Vellan whom he would self-name to. The book says Thulasi asked, and ch 20 echoes this with 'the girl'.
open_errors.fix: Make Kuttu the asker in ch 17 and adjust Vellan's echo in ch 20.

patches.find: "Thulasi asked me."
patches.replace: "Kuttu asked me."

patches.find: "No," he said. "I told the girl once."
patches.replace: "No," he said. "I told the lad once."

open_errors.issue: Neela misremembers two scenes. The ch 3 vote that sent her south was held in the morning, not at night. In the shelter (ch 1) Devan said 'If the hands say no, I sit by this fire and hate it', with no pebble, not 'I go where the hands send me'.
open_errors.fix: Correct the time of the vote and the quoted line.

patches.find: She had watched him do it the night the hands sent her south.
patches.replace: She had watched him do it the morning the hands sent her south.

patches.find: He had said so himself, in the shelter, with a pebble in his cheek and no office: *I go where the hands send me.*
patches.replace: He had said so himself, in the shelter, with no office: *If the hands say no, I sit by this fire and hate it.*

open_errors.issue: Neela ate the sweet in Chathu's lamplit cell, and it tasted 'perfect', which was what she could not forgive (ch 13). Ch 18 says she ate it in the dark and that it turned to ash at once.
open_errors.fix: Align the ch 18 recollection with ch 13.

patches.find: She had eaten one, in the dark, standing, and the sweetness had gone to ash on her tongue at once.
patches.replace: She had eaten one, in his cell, standing, and it had been perfect, and that was the worst of it.

open_errors.issue: In ch 17 Devan reads the queen's letter and writes his refusal on the shelf, on the lid of the arrow cart. In ch 21 he says he stood in the gate chamber, wrote at 'that table', and that Muthu asked him in the yard.
open_errors.fix: Move his recollection to the shelf and the cart lid.

patches.find: "Muthu asked me in the yard if it hurt," he said.
patches.replace: "Muthu asked me on the shelf if it hurt," he said.

patches.find: Her letter said *Kettamala restored,* and I stood in the gate chamber and smelled the pepper on the terraces and I wanted it back.
patches.replace: Her letter said *Kettamala restored,* and I stood on the shelf and smelled the pepper coming down the cut and I wanted it back.

patches.find: I wrote my refusal at that table, and my hand didn't shake
patches.replace: I wrote my refusal on the lid of an arrow cart, and my hand didn't shake

open_errors.issue: The queen gave Neela Usha's fresh page in ch 16, and Neela displays it in ch 20. Yet the queen's case of thirty fresh pages also holds Usha's (it burns in her lap in ch 24). The original intake rolls went to the twenty-two guards in ch 16, so the fresh pages cannot carry them.
open_errors.fix: Have the queen say Usha's page was written twice, and make the looped rolls clerk's copies.

patches.find: Thirty stiff pale leaves lay on blue cloth, each with its intake roll looped on in green thread.
patches.replace: Thirty stiff pale leaves lay on blue cloth, each with a clerk's copy of its intake roll looped on in green thread.

patches.find: Fresh pages, in my own hand, written the night before your wife left Kodiyur.
patches.replace: Fresh pages, in my own hand, written the night before your wife left Kodiyur. Usha's I wrote twice; your wife carries the first.

open_errors.issue: Devan already sparred Muthu in book 2 ch 9 (F720), his first round in eight years. Muthu's claim that the round has been owed 'eight years and a bit' (ch 23) and 'eight years and one month' (ch 32) contradicts this.
open_errors.fix: Date the debt from book 2, and from ch 23 in ch 32.

patches.find: "I've owed it eight years and a bit. I'd like the interest in blood."
patches.replace: "You've owed it since the Resin House. I'd like the interest in blood."

patches.find: "Seventh day," Muthu announced. "I've been owed a round for eight years and one month."
patches.replace: "Seventh day," Muthu announced. "I've been owed a whole round for a month."

open_errors.issue: The 'Sold to the crown' sheet from the sealed last quire travels in Devan's pack (F656, F711), and the leads opened it at the end of book 2. In ch 31 it appears in the queen's green case without explanation.
open_errors.fix: Say Devan laid it in the case.

patches.find: Beside them lay the sheet headed *Sold to the crown*, with thirty ledger numbers and the folded-wing birds.
patches.replace: Beside them lay the sheet headed *Sold to the crown*, which Devan had taken from his pack and laid there at dawn, with thirty ledger numbers and the folded-wing birds.

open_errors.issue: In ch 28 Kandan signed directly under Devan's name, so there is no free line below the two names in ch 31. The outline places 'Bound by choice' beside their names.
open_errors.fix: Put the line in the margin beside the names.

patches.find: Below the two names there was room for one more line.
patches.replace: Beside the two names, in the margin, there was room for one more line.

patches.find: She took the reed, and under their names, in her own steadier letters
patches.replace: She took the reed, and beside their names, in her own steadier letters

open_errors.issue: A guard 'of forty' is among the thirty bought as children. The charter (ch 31) and F715 give the sales as running over twenty years, so no guard sold as a child can be forty.

patches.find: A man of forty with a soldier's walk was a fisherman's son
patches.replace: A man of thirty with a soldier's walk was a fisherman's son
